subject: mathematics
question_text: If A is the matrix with rows (2, −1, 2) and (1, 3, −4), and B is the matrix with rows (1, −2), (−3, 0) and (5, 4), then verify that (AB)′ = B′A′.

recall_prompt: Say how you would verify this — say what you work out on each side.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find (AB)′
steps.margin_note: First mark. Multiply A by B first — a 2×3 times a 3×2 gives a 2×2 — then transpose that result. Do not transpose before multiplying.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply FIRST, then transpose. A 2×3 times a 3×2 gives a 2×2.

recall.must_convey: That AB is computed first (2×3 times 3×2 gives 2×2) and then transposed to give the left-hand side.
accept: multiply A by B first to get a two by two then transpose it
find A B and then take its transpose for the left hand side
the product comes first and the transpose after
modata AB multiply chesi, tarvata transpose teeskovali
A B is two by two and its transpose is the LHS

steps.why: Transposing after multiplying is what the left-hand side literally says. Transposing first would be answering a different question.
common_mistakes: Transposing A and B before multiplying.
Multiplying B by A, which here is a 3×3 and not comparable.

steps.label: Find B′A′ and compare
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Note the ORDER reverses — B′ comes first. B′ is 2×3 and A′ is 3×2, so the product is 2×2 and matches. Written the other way round the sizes would not even fit.
steps.memory_tip: The ORDER reverses: B′ comes first. Written the other way round the sizes would not even fit.

recall.must_convey: That B′A′ is computed with the order REVERSED, and that it equals (AB)′ so the result is verified.
accept: multiply B dash by A dash in that reversed order and it gives the same matrix so the result is verified
the order reverses so B dash comes first, and both sides agree
B dash A dash equals the same two by two so LHS equals RHS
order reverse avthundi, B dash modata, rendu sides same
both sides give fifteen minus twenty eight and four minus eighteen

steps.why: The reversal is the whole content of the rule. A′B′ is not even defined here — a 3×2 times a 2×3 gives a 3×3 — so the order is forced, not a convention.
common_mistakes: Verifying only that the two sides "look similar" without computing both.

insider_note: The order REVERSES: (AB)′ = B′A′, never A′B′, which would not even be defined here. Both sides have to be computed separately and shown equal.
